anti_overlap: fd-swift-python-ipc owns the HTTP boundary between Swift and FastAPI. fd-filesystem-project-model owns corpus file structure on disk. This agent owns only the Claude API integration pattern, context management, and session continuity.
decision_lens: Every research dialogue design decision is evaluated against: what happens when the corpus exceeds the context window? How is session state preserved across app restarts? What is the failure mode when the API is unavailable?
focus: Stateful Claude API integration for the interactive research dialogue surface: context window management, corpus injection strategy, session continuity, and artifact persistence.
name: fd-claude-research-integration
persona: An AI application engineer who has built production systems on the Claude API, understands context window limits, tool use patterns, and the specific failure modes of long-running research dialogue sessions with large document corpora.
review_areas: Context window strategy: the research corpus compounds with every episode — at scale, research/ may contain hundreds of documents far exceeding any context window. Is there a retrieval-augmented approach (embed + retrieve relevant chunks) or does the brainstorm assume full-corpus injection?

Stateful dialogue: 'Socratic exploration' implies multi-turn conversation with memory of prior exchanges. Does the Swift app maintain the messages array client-side, or proxy through FastAPI which manages session state? The brainstorm mentions both direct SDK use and proxy options without resolving the question.

Transcript-to-artifact pipeline: dialogue transcripts become research artifacts added to the corpus. What prevents circular retrieval (a transcript from session N being injected into session N+1 and amplifying its own claims)?

API availability and offline use: if the Claude API is unreachable (no internet, rate limited), does the research surface degrade gracefully — allowing corpus browsing and script editing — or does the entire surface become unusable?

Tool use for corpus search: a Socratic dialogue agent likely needs to search the corpus during conversation. Is there a tool use schema for corpus retrieval that the API can call, and does the FastAPI layer expose this as a callable endpoint?

Cost and token management: interactive research dialogue can generate high token volumes. Is there a token budget visible to the user, a maximum turn length, or a session summarization strategy to compress context?

severity_examples.condition: If there is no plan for semantic chunking, embedding, and retrieval-augmented injection as the corpus grows
severity_examples.scenario: After 20 research sessions, the corpus is too large to inject into context; the brainstorm has no retrieval strategy, so the research surface silently degrades to using only recent documents

severity_examples.condition: If the brainstorm does not resolve whether Claude session state lives in the app or in the FastAPI layer that skills also use
severity_examples.scenario: The Swift app calls the Claude API directly with the Anthropic Swift SDK, bypassing FastAPI — but Claude Code skills also call Claude through a different session, creating two independent conversation histories with no shared state

severity_examples.condition: If transcript auto-save is not specified as a background write on every assistant turn
severity_examples.scenario: A 45-minute research dialogue session is lost when the app is force-quit, because transcript persistence to disk only happens on explicit user save

success_hints: The brainstorm resolves the direct-SDK vs. proxy question, specifies a retrieval strategy for large corpora, defines transcript auto-save on every turn, and names a graceful degradation path when the API is unavailable.
task_context: The brainstorm identifies research dialogue as first-class and lists it as an open question — but marks it as open without resolving even the basic architecture (app vs. proxy). This is the highest-novelty surface in the app and the one most likely to have a subtle design flaw that is expensive to fix after implementation.
